prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
**Goal** — Rebuild Hokusai's "The Great Wave off Kanagawa" (public domain) as a single-file low-poly 3D wallpaper with gentle motion.

**Action** — Inspected `./print.jpg` visually: it is Hokusai's Great Wave, 3 fishing boats, Mt. Fuji. Built `./scene/index.html` (one file, all geometry in code, no textures, only the allowed three.js CDN import) and `./result.json`.

**Result** — Verified in browser: the scene renders the print's composition and palette at a glance — the great curling wave with clawed foam upper-left, layered indigo sea filling the lower half, Mt. Fuji small and snow-capped low in the trough (right of centre), and three low-poly boats (left under the wave, centre in the trough, right climbing the swell) with hunched crews. Palette matches the print: aged-paper sky, deep/mid/light indigo waves, off-white foam, wood hulls, blue Fuji. Gentle motion: wave breathing/rotating, boats bobbing and rocking, Fuji drifting.

**How I know it's right** — I opened the file in a browser (no build step) and read the rendered frame against the reference: wave position, Fuji position/size, and the three-boat layout all match the print; the foam now fans along the crest (not a ring). `result.json` records boats=3 and mountain=Mount Fuji, plus the palette and composition I took from the print.

**Assumptions** — "Low poly" = flat-shaded faceted geometry (cones, torus, displaced plane); "gentle motion" = slow sinusoidal bob/rock/breathe; the print is the reference for composition/palette/subjects, not used as a texture.

**Open limits** — The 3D reading is a stylized low-poly interpretation, not a literal copy of the print's intricate foam line-work; recognizability rests on the wave + Fuji + 3-boats layout and palette, which I confirmed visually.

Browser tab closed.
